How Far Must a ₹4,000 Stock Move Before I Make Money? (FYERS charges + slippage)

On this page

  1. 1. FYERS charges (NSE cash equity, as modelled)
  2. 2. Break-even move for a ₹4,000 stock (bought at ₹4,000)
  3. 3. What it means

Computed Oct 2026 with the same FYERS cost model the backtests use (../../../projects/trading-equation-backtests/src/costs.py). Verify current rates on the FYERS brokerage calculator. Education, not investment advice.

1. FYERS charges (NSE cash equity, as modelled)

ChargeIntradayDelivery
Brokerage₹20 or 0.03% per order, whichever is lower₹20 or 0.3% per order, whichever is lower
STT0.025% on the sell side0.1% on buy and sell
Stamp duty0.003% on the buy0.015% on the buy
NSE transaction fee~0.0031% of buy + sellsame
SEBI fee0.0001% of buy + sellsame
GST18% of (brokerage + exchange + SEBI fees)same
DP chargenone₹14.75 per stock on the sell day
Slippage (not a fee: the price you get is worse than the price you saw)0.02% per side used in backtests; 0.05% for less liquid stockssame

2. Break-even move for a ₹4,000 stock (bought at ₹4,000)

Intraday (slippage 0.02% per side → 0.05% in brackets)

SharesTrade valueBreak-even sell priceMove needed
1–10up to ₹40k₹4,005.9 (₹4,008.3)₹5.9 = 0.15% (₹8.3 = 0.21%)
25₹1L₹4,004.9 (₹4,007.3)₹4.9 = 0.12% (0.18%)
100₹4L₹4,003.5 (₹4,005.9)₹3.5 = 0.09% (0.15%)
250₹10L₹4,003.2 (₹4,005.6)₹3.2 = 0.08% (0.14%)

Delivery (slippage 0.02% per side → 0.05% in brackets)

SharesTrade valueBreak-even sell priceMove needed
1₹4k₹4,053.8 (₹4,056.3)₹54 = 1.35% (DP ₹14.75 + brokerage hurt small trades)
10₹40k₹4,016.7 (₹4,019.1)₹16.7 = 0.42% (0.48%)
25₹1L₹4,013.0 (₹4,015.4)₹13 = 0.33% (0.39%)
100₹4L₹4,011.1 (₹4,013.5)₹11.1 = 0.28% (0.34%)
250₹10L₹4,010.8 (₹4,013.2)₹10.8 = 0.27% (0.33%)

A short (intraday) needs the same size move down.

3. What it means

  • Rule of thumb: intraday ≈ 0.1–0.2% (₹4–8 on ₹4,000); delivery ≈ 0.3–0.4% (₹11–16) once the trade is ₹40k+. Below ~₹20k per trade, the flat ₹20 brokerage and ₹14.75 DP charge make delivery much more expensive in %.
  • Delivery costs more per trade because of STT (0.1% on both sides vs 0.025% on the sell only), but delivery trades aim for 2–10% moves, so 0.3% is small. Intraday aims for 0.3–1% moves, so 0.15% is a big share of the target.
  • Break-even is not profit. It covers the costs only. Your average winner must beat this, and win rate × average win must beat loss rate × average loss + costs (break-even win rate p* = (avg loss + costs) / (avg win + avg loss), see trader_returns_reality.md).
  • Example: intraday target ₹20 (0.5%), stop ₹10 on ₹4,000 → costs ₹6 per trade. Net win ₹14, net loss ₹16 → you need a win rate above 16 / (14 + 16) = 53%, not 33%.
  • Tax is extra: short-term delivery gains 20%; intraday profit is taxed at your slab rate.
